claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit in the UK.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old. I'd like to know if I'm eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with things like clothes and other expenses - I give about £26 a week towards looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know you're contributing £26 a week.

**Can you tell me - does Alex live with someone else who might also be claiming Child Benefit for him (such as his other parent, a relative, or another guardian)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex in any of these situations:**
- In hospital or residential accommodation?
- In care provided by the local council?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in hospital or any residential accommodation, and he's not in council care either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

**You mentioned you contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's upkeep. How long has this arrangement been in place - has Alex been living with someone else for more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex has been living with his other parent for quite a while now - definitely more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me clarify one important point:

**You mentioned the other parent is not claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Are you certain about this, or is it possible they might be claiming it without you knowing?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child, and typically if a child lives with someone, that person would be the one claiming.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm certain - the other parent isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you are still considered responsible for him because you're contributing £26 per week towards his upkeep (through clothes and other expenses). The rules state that you can qualify for Child Benefit if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after the child. Since the Child Benefit rate for one child is approximately £25.60 per week, your £26 weekly contribution meets this threshold.

Additionally:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation

**Important things to note:**
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so as long as no one else claims for Alex, you can continue to receive it
- You'll need to continue making contributions of at least the Child Benefit amount to maintain eligibility
- If your income or your partner's income exceeds £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the government website or by contacting HMRC.
